hints: Each desired route is a unit of flow, but the output must list the actual edge-disjoint routes.
Compute maximum flow with unit edge capacities while storing residual edges.
For each unit of flow, extract one path using edges with positive flow, then remove that unit from the extracted flow.
analogy: First find how many nonoverlapping routes fit, then peel those routes out of the flow assignment.
example: If the flow is 2, output two paths that share no directed edge, even if they share cities.
algorithm: Run max-flow with capacity 1 on each directed connection. Decompose the resulting integral flow into source-to-sink paths by DFS over edges carrying flow, subtracting one unit after each extraction.
correctness: Integral max flow decomposes into unit source-to-sink paths plus cycles; extracting the source-sink paths yields the reported edge-disjoint routes.
complexity: O(V^2E) with Edmonds-Karp plus path extraction; O(V+E) storage.
